subject.title: Feature: groupScope option to consolidate group sessions into main

question: Should OpenClaw support folding group input into an agent’s main session only through explicit fully matched bindings, or also provide a global `session.groupScope: "main"` default?
rationale: Both shapes are new compatibility-sensitive configuration surfaces, but the global form broadens group-to-main context sharing beyond the selective trusted-group use case and therefore needs maintainer intent rather than an automated choice.

options.title: Sponsor explicit binding opt-in
options.body: Approve a narrow per-binding group-to-main setting for explicitly matched peers, keeping the global default isolated and documenting the shared-context trust consequence.

options.title: Approve symmetric global scope
options.body: Accept `session.groupScope: "main"` as a deliberate operator-wide choice, with per-binding overrides and prominent trust-boundary documentation.

options.title: Defer to broader shared-session design
options.body: Pause this focused implementation until the policy and configuration model in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/19929 is selected as the canonical direction.

recommendation.title: Sponsor explicit binding opt-in
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow per-binding group-to-main setting for explicitly matched peers, keeping the global default isolated and documenting the shared-context trust consequence.

likelyOwner.reason: The available routing and session-history evidence most strongly connects this person to the current main implementation and the required product-boundary decision.
